title: Nvidia Open Sources Run:ai to End GPU Scheduling Lock In
summary:
The GPU orchestration platform Run:ai is now available as open source software through Nvidia's DSX AI Factory Platform. This allows developers and partners to build production-grade AI workloads to improve GPU utilization and increase throughput for AI factory solutions. Users can choose to deploy the integrated system or adopt individual components according to their needs.

Cloud providers such as Lambda have supported the software since 2022 and integrate it alongside Slurm, Kubernetes, and SkyPilot. Opening the source code allows managed-service providers to package and test the tools more easily and ensures users are not locked into one specific method of scheduling GPUs.

Today, we’re open sourcing the full NVIDIA Run:ai platform as part of the NVIDIA DSX AI Factory Platform.

Developers, platform teams, and partners can build on production-grade AI workloads and GPU orchestration to improve GPU utilization, increase workload throughput, and bring AI factory solutions to market faster.

Deploy the integrated NVIDIA Run:ai platform or adopt individual components to fit your needs.

See what’s included, how to get started, and how to contribute: https://t.co/2DB9gjjdYD

selectedTweets.text:
NVIDIA just open-sourced Run:ai. Good news if you'd rather not be locked into one way of scheduling GPUs.

Run:ai is one of several orchestrators you can run on Lambda, alongside Slurm, Kubernetes, and SkyPilot. You pick how to allocate and share your GPUs. We keep them healthy underneath, node-level auto-remediation ships in Lambda Kubernetes Service today.

We've supported Run:ai on Lambda since 2022. Open source makes it easier to package, test, and keep it current as a managed option.

Read more: https://t.co/QvBsSa2ZAV
